source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Hypocalcemia because potassium-containing salt substitutes prevent intestinal calcium absorption","B":"Hypokalemia because combining an ACE inhibitor with spironolactone causes excessive potassium loss","C":"Hypernatremia because spironolactone directly increases sodium retention when combined with an ACE inhibitor","D":"Hyperkalemia because the medicines and potassium-containing salt substitute can all raise potassium"}}
source_row.rationale: ACE inhibitors can increase serum potassium, and spironolactone is potassium-sparing. Potassium supplements or potassium-containing salt substitutes add further risk, so serum potassium and renal function require monitoring.
source_row.source_detail: Current label accessed 2026-08-14: hyperkalemia risk increases with potassium supplements, potassium-containing salt substitutes, and drugs that increase potassium such as ACE inhibitors; serum potassium monitoring is required.
source_row.source_name: DailyMed — Spironolactone Tablets, Warnings and Precautions 5.1 Hyperkalemia
source_row.stem: A client takes an ACE inhibitor and spironolactone and also uses a potassium-chloride salt substitute. Which complication is the priority concern?
